title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls, result injection, and retry handling
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Customers are increasingly invoking multiple tools per request and expect predictable execution semantics when tools run in parallel, when tool results are injected back into the model, and when transient tool failures require retries. This PR improves the runtime ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel tool-calling workflows, stabilizes streaming when tool results are injected mid-response, and adds explicit retry policies and metrics so platform users and infra can reason about cost and correctness.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a ToolExecutionManager in the serving runtime to coordinate parallel tool invocations and deterministic result injection order.
- Adds an opt-in "tool_retry_policy" on the API surface that supports (none|idempotent|best_effort) semantics and configurable backoff/retry limits.
- Ensures the streaming layer remains stable when tool results are interleaved into an ongoing token stream by buffering and inserting result boundaries; reduces duplicate partial events.
- Emits per-request tool call traces and metrics (tool_calls.count, tool_calls.retries, tool_calls.latency_p50/95) consumed by Redwood Console and the observability pipeline.
- Extends the OpenAI compatibility layer mapping so that function_call semantics map to our multi-tool model: the compatibility layer now exposes `tool_execution` metadata and preserves order for multi-tool calls coming from OpenAI-style `function_call` payloads.

Why: Customers running agent-style workflows reported edge cases: non-deterministic injection order for parallel tools, streaming observers receiving malformed/duplicate partial events when a tool resolved and injected results mid-stream, and unclear platform-level semantics for retrying transient tool failures. These issues manifested as flaky outputs, higher token counts due to duplicated partial generation, and debugging difficulty.

Checklist: 
- [x] Serving runtime orchestration for parallel tool calls
- [x] API contract addition (tool_retry_policy) and OpenAI compat mapping update
- [x] Streaming stability fixes + unit/integration tests
- [x] Observability metrics + Console dashboard patch
- [x] Docs and examples updated (TS/Python SDK snippets)

Commit summary: See commits field for short list.

Compatibility/migration: The new fields are opt-in. Existing customers see no behavior change unless they explicitly set `tool_retry_policy` or enable parallel tool execution via the `tools[*].parallel` flag. OpenAI compatibility requests that include multiple function calls now map deterministically to our tool execution graph; warnings are emitted if the incoming payload relies on unspecified ordering.

CI: Multiple test suites were added to cover race conditions and stream boundary insertion. A flaky integration test in perf-canary was quarantined and tracked as ENG-4289.

Files changed: See changed_files; this is a relatively focused change touching the runtime coordinator, streaming layer, API schema, SDK adapters, and documentation.

Notes for reviewers: Pay particular attention to the idempotency semantics in runtime/tool_manager.go and the OpenAI-compat mapping in api/openai_adapter.go. The buffering logic in streaming/stream_inserter.go has subtle boundaries to preserve low-latency streaming while guaranteeing correct final output.

Merge outcome: Squash merge to main after approvals and green CI.
release_notes: Improved tool-calling ergonomics: deterministic ordering for parallel tool calls, opt-in retry policies, streaming stability when injecting tool results, and observability metrics for tool calls.

motivation_short: Make multi-tool, parallel, and retry semantics predictable and observable so agent-style workflows are reliable in production.
test_plan: Unit tests for ToolExecutionManager and stream inserter; e2e simulating parallel tools with injected delays; QA ran agent smoke tests against dedicated staging; perf micro-bench added to ensure <5% P50 overhead for streaming in common path.
rollout_notes: Feature is opt-in by default. To enable parallel tool execution set tools[*].parallel=true in the request. To enable retries, set tool_retry_policy in request. Console dashboard will surface tool_calls.* metrics after deployment.
notes: Follow-up: consider exposing a high-level SDK helper for composing multi-tool workflows that encodes idempotency keys automatically (tracked ENG-4328).
